about: One pinned short that shows how to read the readout (src/scenes/Readout.tsx), which 35 shorts use. The user, 2026-09-27: 'we probably need an explainer video then for each of the styles? or are all of the styles pretty self explanatory except for the nostromo wang bi shorts'. The example is 22 Grace: line 5 is yin, OUT of place, yet a centre and the master.
look: The readout's own screen with 22's plot, fully built from the start, without the lesson line. Step text sits above the header. The part a step explains goes to full green while the rest dims; amber only where the real screen uses it (◄ lines and the WANG BI line), in the last two steps.

steps.lights: plot and log; L1 first, then upward
steps.text:
SIX LINES, L1
AT THE BOTTOM.

steps.lights: L1 (solid) and L2 (broken) and their YANG/YIN words
steps.text:
SOLID LINE: YANG.
BROKEN LINE: YIN.

steps.lights: the IN/OUT column: L1 L3 L5, then L2 L4 L6
steps.text:
ODD PLACES WANT
YANG, EVEN YIN.

steps.lights: L2 YIN IN, then L5 YIN OUT
steps.text:

WRONG KIND: OUT.

steps.lights: the left bracket with L1 (YANG) and L4 (YIN); then L2+L5 (both YIN) and L3+L6 (both YANG) briefly, no bracket
the UPPER row with L4-L6 and its bracket, then the LOWER row with L1-L3 and its bracket
the right brackets, then L2 and L5 with · CENTRE
L2 and L5 amber with ◄, and the finding

TO LOOK AT.

steps.lights: > WANG BI: 為飾之主 / MASTER OF ADORNMENT, and L5
steps.text:
WANG BI NAMES THE
LINE THAT RULES.

caption: How to read the green screen in 35 of our shorts, using 22 Grace. The Ten Wings judge each line as in or out of its place; Wang Bi (AD 226–249) applied this only to lines 2 to 5.
